issues.summary: Blueprint places the 7 new ADRs (ADR-0044..ADR-0050) at working/feature/issue-capture-mechanism-r1/adrs/, contradicting both ADR-0036 (single-location ADR placement) AND the synthesis ADR Slate Placement Constraint
issues.description: ADR-0036 (status: accepted) Decision: 'Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) live in exactly one canonical location: the project-wide registry at adrs/ADR-NNNN-<title>.md at the repository root. No feature-scoped duplicate is required, expected, or recommended... Do NOT create working/feature/<slug>/adrs/ directories or duplicate ADR files.' Synthesis §ADR Slate Placement Constraint reinforces this verbatim: 'All 7 ADRs land in /workspaces/feature-pipeline/adrs/ per ADR-0036.' Yet the Blueprint authored all 7 ADRs at working/feature/issue-capture-mechanism-r1/adrs/. Verified by direct ls: /workspaces/feature-pipeline/adrs/ADR-0044* through ADR-0050* return 'No such file or directory'; /workspaces/feature-pipeline/working/feature/issue-capture-mechanism-r1/adrs/ contains all seven. The Blueprint's §References > ADR placement note acknowledges this and defers to 'the prompt's directive and the still-current operational convention pending ADR-0036 amendment propagation' — but no superseding ADR exists per ADR-0005, and Blueprint §Background and Context Prerequisite ADRs claims ADR-0036 'applies to the 7 new ADRs authored this run'. The ADR-0036 Kill Criteria (3+ feature runs surfacing operational need for feature-scoped copies) is NOT the basis cited; the cited basis is an external 'prompt directive'.

evidence.excerpt: ADRs live only at adrs/ADR-NNNN-<title>.md. No feature-scoped duplicate. Do NOT create working/feature/<slug>/adrs/ directories or duplicate ADR files.
All 7 ADRs land in /workspaces/feature-pipeline/adrs/ per ADR-0036.

No such file or directory (all 7 ADRs absent from canonical /adrs/)

issues.recommended_resolution: Three viable paths: (a) MOVE the 7 ADR files from working/feature/<slug>/adrs/ to /adrs/ per ADR-0036's Decision (this would also align with the synthesis claim and remove the cross-document inconsistency); (b) author a superseding ADR per ADR-0005 that amends ADR-0036 to permit feature-scoped ADR authoring during pipeline runs (with deliverable-packager later canonicalizing to /adrs/) — this would require Stage-7 design-composer to author the superseding ADR per FR-5; (c) escalate to the user with an explicit user-disposition recorded in the Blueprint frontmatter (e.g., user_token_for_adr_placement_deviation) and a corresponding revision to the synthesis claim. Path (a) is the cleanest brief-honor resolution. Path (b) requires honest documentation of the architectural drift as a new ADR. The current 'captured drift' framing in Blueprint §References is insufficient because it neither resolves the contradiction nor authors a superseding decision record.

issues.summary: ADR-0044 commits 'evidence/ and updates/ subdirectories explicitly excluded from FR-7's validator extension' but the Blueprint's Backend Design does not specify the exclusion mechanism; current validator emits minor finding on agent-roster-impact-matrix.md (verified empirically) which will persist after FR-9 migration into Issues/.../evidence/ unless the validator extension adds a path-prefix skip
issues.description: ADR-0044 Decision item 4 (line 61): 'A topic folder MAY contain these two subdirectories for non-doctype artifacts. Files inside evidence/ and updates/ are NOT validated as doctype files and MAY carry any frontmatter shape. They are explicitly excluded from FR-7's validator extension.' ADR-0044 Implementation Guidance (line 149): 'Files under Issues/<topic-slug>/evidence/ and Issues/<topic-slug>/updates/ are skipped (no doctype validation applied).' However, the Blueprint's Backend Design §Service/Module Layout (lines 850-857), §Corrected Pseudocode Reference (lines 887-921), §Data Contract (lines 687-713), and §Field Propagation Map do NOT describe any path-prefix skip for Issues/<topic>/evidence/ or Issues/<topic>/updates/. The validator extension's dispatch is by doc_type_category returning 'issue' when doc_type ∈ ISSUE_DOC_TYPES. The migrated agent-roster-impact-matrix.md (FR-9 target) carries doc_type: agent-roster-impact-matrix (not in any known category), so it currently produces a minor 'doc_type ... not in known category' finding (verified empirically via python3 validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py on the current path). Post-FR-9 migration into Issues/per-agent-design-evaluation-gap/evidence/, the same minor finding will persist unless the validator extension explicitly path-prefix-skips evidence/ and updates/ subdirectories. The Blueprint provides no such mechanism. This is a cross-section inconsistency: the new ADR makes a commitment the new Backend Design does not honor.

issues.recommended_resolution: Amend the Blueprint's Backend Design to specify the exclusion mechanism. Two viable approaches: (a) extend the outer dispatch at validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py lines 365-371 with a path-prefix check that skips files under /evidence/ or /updates/ inside Issues/, returning an empty finding list before reaching validate_pipeline_artifact (e.g., 'if "/Issues/" in str_path and ("/evidence/" in str_path or "/updates/" in str_path): return []'); (b) extend validate_pipeline_artifact's unknown-category branch (lines 304-312) to skip files whose path matches Issues/<topic>/(evidence|updates)/ rather than emit a minor finding. Either approach honors ADR-0044's commitment. Without this fix, the Blueprint's claim that ADR-0044 is fully implemented by FR-7 is false, and AC-FR-9-b (agent-roster-impact-matrix migration produces no validator regression) is at risk of failing post-migration. Note: this does NOT affect NFR-8 zero-blocker backward compatibility (the finding is minor), but it does contradict ADR-0044's explicit commitment and may surface as a Plan-stage defect.

verdict_rationale: No BLOCKER issues. Two MAJOR issues: (I-AA-001) Inherited-ADR contradiction with ADR-0036 — the 7 new ADRs are placed at working/feature/<slug>/adrs/ rather than the canonical /adrs/, contradicting both ADR-0036 (accepted) AND the synthesis claim that '/All 7 ADRs land in /workspaces/feature-pipeline/adrs/ per ADR-0036'. The Blueprint acknowledges this drift but does not author a superseding ADR per ADR-0005. (I-AA-002) Cross-section inconsistency between ADR-0044 (commits to evidence/updates exclusion from validator) and Blueprint Backend Design (no exclusion mechanism specified; agent-roster-impact-matrix.md will produce a minor finding post-migration). Three MINOR issues are stale-wording or citation-accuracy nits localizable to specific lines (Interface Change Matrix 'or' phrasing, ADR-0047 applies_to four-vs-five inconsistency, AC-FR-11-c citation). Five INFO observations document audit-positive findings (F-003 mitigation rigorous; pipeline-isolation invariant verified at zero-baseline; all 14 decision frames addressed; all Q-CC/Q-BE items dispositioned; Blueprint doc_type omission is a pre-existing template drift). Per the severity rules, MAJOR-without-BLOCKER → conditional_pass — finalize-reconciler may dispatch revision (recommended for I-AA-001 and I-AA-002, which are auditor-driven reconciliation candidates not requiring user gate) or surface to user with rationale to defer the I-AA-001 ADR placement question if the orchestrator's prior 'prompt directive' is the binding source.
